used_sources.name: Python documentation passages curated in CodeGuard
used_sources.relevance: Primary Python semantics evidence; claim wording is synthetic.
used_sources.limitations: The repository's existing 12 short passages, not the complete Python documentation.

candidates.name: FEVER
candidates.license: Wikipedia article terms or CC BY-SA 3.0 where terms unavailable (official notice)
candidates.evidence_present: Evidence sets for supported/refuted; NEI uses null evidence references.
candidates.relevance: General textual claim verification, but Wikipedia subject domain is unlike Python documentation.
candidates.mapping: Potential label mapping exists, but evidence must be dereferenced and converted; NEI placeholder is not evidence text.
candidates.limitations: Out-of-domain; Wikipedia-derived source/licensing obligations; excluded from final data.

candidates.name: SciFact
candidates.license: Claims/evidence annotations CC BY 4.0; abstract corpus ODC-By 1.0
candidates.relevance: Claim/evidence shape is close, but biomedical subject matter is not Python semantics.
candidates.mapping: SUPPORT→SUPPORTED, CONTRADICT→CONTRADICTED; no reliable INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE class in the released labeled claims.
candidates.limitations: Different domain and label coverage; corpus text has a separate ODC-By license; excluded.

exclusion_policy: No dataset was added solely for scale. Candidates must have relevant domain, usable claim plus evidence text, mappable labels, and clear source terms.
